text: The Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables governs the ownership of all 93 tables. The 92 recovery tables and the 4 extension tables of version 3 are kept as printed and no total is derived from them, because the two counts differ by three tables.
why: Version 3 counts 92 plus 4; the map holds 93 rows including the 6 platform library tables. Test data must be seeded per owner, and the map is the only source that assigns an owner to every table.
read: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Data Plan v3.docx section 6; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx sheet Tables; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json tables.
applied_in: Section 2 (Recovery tables row and the table count sentence) and section 6 (Recovery tables and Tables owned rows).
impact: If a later count fixes the total, the two rows of section 6 change and no other text does.

text: rwb-valuation (S1) keeps no table. Its route decision reads valuation_ext through the rwb-source-data contract and records each RouteDecided outcome as a decision record in rwb_decision (P7).
why: The Ownership Map assigns no table to S1 and version 3 lists valuation among the 20 removed tables, so the plan cannot seed a valuation schema.
read: Ownership Map v1 sheets Services and Tables; Architecture v5 slides 13, 41 and 43; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json tables.
applied_in: Section 2.1, row S1; section 3.1, row S1.
impact: If a technical specification adds a valuation table, the row gains a seed statement and the fake of S1 serves the stored rows.

text: The contract fakes are hosted by a stub server generated from the published artefact, run in the build pipeline. The product is not chosen in this document; the choice belongs to the CON story of each provider.
why: Architecture v5 slide 11 requires the artefact before the code and a contract test in every build, but no source names a mock product or environment.
read: Architecture v5 slides 11, 20 and 46; Template and Rules v1 R5.4.
impact: If a product is mandated, only the first rule of section 3.1 changes; the fake table stays as it is.

text: One key set is shared by the seed and every fake: caseId, accountId and partyKey identify the same row on both sides of a contract, and each fake is loaded from the seed file of its provider.
why: Version 3 has one data set. With 19 services a consumer test sees a fake, so the keys must be the same or the test proves nothing about the pair.
read: Version 3 sections 2 and 3; Architecture v5 slide 11 (key caseId, Idempotency-Key); Template and Rules v1 R5.4 class C.
impact: If a provider already uses a different key, the fake maps the key and the seed is not changed.

text: rwb-access (P4) holds the approved masking version as masking_rule; rwb-source-data (P1) applies the mask at the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views; the service that owns a personal field applies display masking at its API under the same version.
why: Version 3 says the rules are data and Compliance approves them, but not which service applies them. The map gives masking_rule to P4 and Architecture v5 slide 46 says masking is applied by rwb-source-data.
read: Version 3 section 4; Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 46.
applied_in: Section 4, first paragraph and the view and display bullets.
impact: If the field owner cannot mask, the mask is applied in rwb-source-data and the API returns the masked value; the bullets change, the rules do not.

text: Each of the 19 services seeds its own schema from its own baseline with seed 20261128, and no service seeds another service's schema. The 2,812 case rows are seeded once, in rwb_case, and every other schema refers to them by plain key.
why: Version 3 seeds one schema from one generator and does not say how a split seed keeps the links. DP-01 forbids a cross-schema foreign key.
read: Version 3 section 2; Architecture v5 slide 29; Template and Rules v1 R5.4 DP-01 and DP-15.
applied_in: Section 2, introduction and closing paragraph; section 2.1, introduction.
impact: If the generator must run once for all schemas, the order of the baseline run changes and the key rule stays.

text: An event that Architecture v5 slide 43 names without a number is cited in this plan by its name and its topic; its EV number is added when the event catalogue owner numbers it.
why: The Ownership Map numbers 30 events and slide 43 adds a further set marked +. A fake needs an identity and the source gives only a name and a topic.
read: Ownership Map v1 sheet Events; Architecture v5 slide 43.
applied_in: Section 3.1, rows P2, P4, S1, S3, S4, S5 and S6.
impact: If numbers are allocated, the rows gain the EV ID and no data changes.

text: The daily journey smoke run (JOB-22, PlatformSmokeWorkflow) uses the DEV seed of all 19 schemas and the fakes, and creates its own case for each journey step so it leaves the seed of the other tests untouched.
why: Version 3 lists no data for the smoke run, and the run crosses every service in one journey.
read: Architecture v5 slides 44 and 46; Ownership Map v1 sheet Jobs (JOB-22); version 3 section 3.
impact: If the smoke run must use SIT, it needs the masked copy and the seed; no other row changes.

text: The decision reference of version 3 (D-RCV-35 (U1, U4); ADR-010; DL43) is restated as D-RCV-60 with ADR-014 (schema and login per service), ADR-020 (contract-first REST, one hop, 2 s) and ADR-021 (per-service Flyway), and DL44 (adopt Architecture v5). The version is 4 under Template and Rules R8.2. Every section, ID, number and date of version 3 is kept.
why: D-RCV-60 supersedes the decision references of version 3 and the family is at version 3, so the next issue is 4.
read: _work/msr/plan/ids.json; Template and Rules v1 R8.2; version 3 metadata table and section 7.
applied_in: Title block, metadata table and section 7.
impact: If another decision ID is allocated, only the metadata row and section 7 change.

text: The document states no release date, so no date is marked tentative. The seed 20261128 and the date 15 November 2026 are kept as printed.
why: Template and Rules R8.1 and the WP require a (tentative) mark on release dates only, and this document carries none.
read: Version 3 title block and metadata table; Template and Rules v1 R8.1, R8.2 and the Day-1 rule set.
applied_in: Metadata table (Date row) and title block line.
impact: If a release date is added later, it carries the (tentative) mark.

text: The four platform library objects outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event and idempotency_key exist in all 19 schemas and are seeded per schema; feature_flag and feature_flag_change exist once, in rwb_integration.
why: The map owns the six tables as PLT and PLT has no schema, while DP-09 and Architecture v5 slide 20 make the outbox and inbox part of every service schema. A test needs an outbox row in the schema that publishes the event.
read: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables and sheet Services; Architecture v5 slide 20; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09.
applied_in: Section 2, Platform library objects row; section 2.1, row PLT; section 6, Platform library objects row.
impact: If the library ships as a shared schema or a library, the seed row per schema and the two count rows change; no service row does.
